findings.minimal_fix: Aggregate resident bytes per canonical device across all shards (e.g. dev_tot[nd] = dev_tot.get(nd, 0) + rb) and verify after the loop that dev_tot[d] <= np[d] for every canonical device d.
findings.reason: Peak allocator coverage is evaluated per-shard individually rather than against the cumulative sum of resident bytes per device. If device0 hosts two 1000-byte shards against a reported allocator peak of 1000 bytes, np.get(nd,0) < rb (1000 < 1000) evaluates false for both, falsely passing an oversubscribed allocation where resident weights (2000 bytes) exceed peak allocator bytes (1000 bytes).

findings.minimal_fix: Compute act_max = max(abs(p['observed'] - p['cpu']) for p in lg) and verify act_max <= mx <= tol, and verify rmse is mathematically consistent with the logit errors (e.g. abs(math.sqrt(sum((p['observed']-p['cpu'])**2 for p in lg)/len(lg)) - rm) <= 1e-6).
findings.reason: Individual logit differences are only compared against the tolerance threshold lt, never against the claimed max_abs_error mx. An execution record claiming rmse: 0.0 and max_abs_error: 0.0 passes even when observed logit differences are 0.05 (within lt=0.1), allowing self-reported clean execution metrics that are directly contradicted by the accompanying logit payload.

findings.minimal_fix: Explicitly require len(ds) == len(canon) == phys for each attempt; if duplicate canonical IDs or duplicate device definitions are provided, immediately fail dedup.
findings.reason: When a device list contains duplicate entries for the same physical GPU, nm & seen is non-empty on subsequent occurrences, preventing phys from incrementing, while canon.add(cid) does not increase len(canon). Consequently, len(canon) == phys remains true, allowing a padded list of duplicate devices to pass the cardinality check (e.g. [dev0, dev0] for role single yields phys=1 and passes single_phys).
